installer: unmodified setup.py from the measured commit, run by the image's docker-entrypoint.sh

model.title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder (ISTA-DASLab's coding version: half of each layer's experts)
model.revision_source: setup.py HF_REVISIONS, the revision the installer pins
model.quantization: IQ1_M (the Coder's only size; experts stored like IQ3_S, ~3.5 bits)

files.role: shard 1: the part loaded at startup (experts to RAM, dense weights to the GPU)
shard 2: the PLE / n-gram table, stays on the SSD
vision encoder (the Coder repository ships the original's mmproj)

hash_command: sha256sum inside the container, compared with the repository's published LFS oids from the Hugging Face API at the pinned revision

mtp_draft_layer.source: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (the BF16 checkpoint's MTP block), fetched by tools/mtp_fetch.py
mtp_draft_layer.note: The manifest carries a SHA-256 per tensor, which the fetcher verifies against the checkpoint's own hashes; the full BF16 shards were not downloaded. The installer then built mtp-q2_0.gguf and the runtime pack under /data/mtp/rt (6.5 GB on disk including the tensors).

prepared_pack.bytes_on_disk: 1.4 GB (the installer's own pack; the experts themselves are served natively from shard 1)

notes: All three model files matched the published hashes byte for byte, so the numbers below are for the published IQ1_M, not for a re-quantized or truncated copy.
The download and the pack preparation were done by the unmodified installer in the official image; nothing was quantized or repacked by hand.
